figures.caption: Figure 4. Chai Differential Testing. End-to-end design of Chai. From a high-level goal, 1) Plan decomposes it into subgoals with RAG over library source and CVEs, 2) Execute mutates and builds candidate inputs for every harness, and 3) Analyze minimizes, classifies, and reports each differential. Findings go to review; results feed back into the loop (dashed).

Figure 10. Per-protocol breakdown of Chai’s differential search. Left: cumulative unique differences against inference cost (USD) with each of the four mutator models of Section 5. Right: the mutation groups (Section 3) that produced the most unique differences.
Figure 11. Detailed capability coverage heatmaps for X.509, JWT, and SAML.

Figure 9. Unique differences found by Chai and baselines per protocol, grouped by the validation behavior each difference exercises. Blank cells indicate categories where a tool surfaced no differences. A higher-fidelity breakdown of each category appears in Appendix A.2.

Figure 6. Unique differences surfaced by Chai and baselines over 1,500 executions, where one execution is a single input (X.509 certificate, JWT, or SAML message) submitted to all harnessed libraries. Annotations give total cost, included only for methods that incur inference or GPU cost.
